feature: account list with signer/writable permissions in the account envelope
question: Which accounts did a transaction touch, and could it write to them?
why_it_mattered: The envelope said WHAT changed and HOW MANY accounts existed (accounts_total/static/loaded), but not WHICH accounts or their signer/writable permissions. A consumer that needed those had to pay a second RPC round trip — the exact cost the envelope exists to remove. This was qualification point 4 of the README's Next-qualification list.

premise_checks_before_coding.encoding_json_accountKeys: Always bare STRINGS for every message, legacy or not — so 'key0 is a string' says nothing about the message version, and encoding json states NO per-key permissions. (This falsified my own first probe, which classified messages as legacy/versioned by key shape.)
premise_checks_before_coding.where_the_authority_lives: encoding jsonParsed states signer/writable/source per key: transaction | lookupTable.
premise_checks_before_coding.yellowstone: Ports 10000 on yellowstone.mainnet.beta.rpcpool.com, yellowstone.grpc.mainnet.solana.com and grpc.mainnet.solana.com all unreachable from this host — qualification point 2 (second transport) cannot be tested here, measured not assumed.

falsification_of_the_derivation_live_bef.method: For each live signature: fetch the same transaction in encoding json (what reeflog stores) and encoding jsonParsed (the RPC's own permissions), derive flags from (header + meta.loadedAddresses groups) exactly as a json consumer must, compare position by position.

artifact.envelope_field: accounts[] — {index, address, signer, writable, source: static|lookup_writable|lookup_readonly}, canonical order preserved (static, loaded writable, loaded readonly)
artifact.flags_source_field: accounts_flags_source: stated (response carries them) | header (derived from the message header's three counts) | unavailable (header missing or counts cannot describe the static keys → accounts is null, permissions REFUSED rather than guessed)
artifact.debt_predicate: events_missing_accounts / accounts_missing_count / accounts_partial / set_accounts all now treat an envelope without accounts_flags_source as half — envelopes written by an older binary are re-enriched instead of quoted back as complete. accounts_flags_source is written even when the derivation is refused (unavailable), so a genuinely un-derivable row is not refetched forever.

falsification_ladder.pre_fix_tree: clone of HEAD before the change + the 5 new test functions inserted into its test module
falsification_ladder.pre_fix_result: 5/5 NEW tests RED (accounts_flags_source null vs expected stated/header/unavailable), 15/15 pre-existing accounts tests GREEN — the old tree is not broken, it is silent about the new field
falsification_ladder.post_fix_result: 90/90 green (84 existing + 6 new: 5 unit + 1 real-transaction fixture test)

offline_regression_against_chain_truth.test: the_derived_account_list_equals_the_authoritative_flags_of_a_real_lookup_table_transaction — compares reeflog's derived list against jsonParsed's authoritative signer/writable/source, address by address
offline_regression_against_chain_truth.why: the e2e's live rows were all static-key transactions; the loaded-account path had no authority offline. The fixture closes that on every CI run, and it asserts the fixture itself actually contains loaded accounts so it cannot silently degenerate into a static-only test.
offline_regression_against_chain_truth.caveat: fixture holds ONE transaction (the loaded path, not a population of them); the live probe above covered 2 lookup-table transactions

live_e2e.harness: tools/e2e-accounts.mjs — cross-check extended to compare the account list field by field against the harness's OWN independent derivation (it does not read reeflog's output)
new_checks: cross-check: stored envelopes (balances, instructions, outcome, account list) equal an independent re-fetch field by field — matched=4 mismatched=0
account list: every enriched row states where its permissions came from, and a stated list is complete — rows=4 withList=4 sources=[header], every list length equals accounts_total

own_errors_found_by_the_measurement.harness_bug_1: The cross-check passed the accountList FUNCTION REFERENCE instead of calling it, so the 'independent' side was always a function object and never equal: matched=0, mismatched=4 with accountListEqual=false while every OTHER field matched. Found because the failure output named accountListEqual specifically while lamports/tokens/instructions/err were all equal — a real product failure would not have been that selective. Fixed by calling the function.
own_errors_found_by_the_measurement.test_bug: My first expectation in the_account_list_carries_the_permissions_a_consumer_needs assumed 1 writable-unsigned key; the header rule gives n_static - n_sig - n_ru = 4 - 1 - 1 = 2. The CODE was right (it matches the derivation measured against jsonParsed); the assertion was wrong and was corrected rather than the implementation bent to the test.

mutations_added: permission-shift — writable bit flipped by index parity (balances untouched, so only the cross-check's account-list comparison can catch it)
loaded-group-swap — a lookup_writable account marked readonly (order stays right, permissions wrong — exactly what the jsonParsed fixture targets)
mutation_probe.result: see proof below — probe prints N/N mutants caught, each exit 1

regressions.sememe_consumer: 193/193 green — the second out-of-tree consumer reads instructions[] and is unaffected by the additive field
regressions.whirlpool_watcher: offline tests untouched (reads logs/fills, not the account list)

false_premise_retracted.claim: README qualification point 1 and the card's next step both said 'my own RFQ fill polling has not been moved over yet — migrate it onto reeflog tail/webhook'
false_premise_retracted.measurement: scanned all 28 repositories of mine on this machine (git remote auroraxo/*) plus the whole home directory outside github_repos for an RFQ fill poller in mjs/js/ts/py/sh/rs: zero matches — no such script, service or file exists. Matches for 'rfq' are documentation, fixtures containing base58 substrings, and vendored third-party code.
false_premise_retracted.verdict: the premise is false, in the same category as the falsified '21 own key-load sites' of 24.10: an inventory sentence never checked against the disk. README corrected (the honest remainder is 'a third party using reeflog', which was always the real gate) and the card's next step replaced.
false_premise_retracted.consequence: the 'migrate the RFQ poller' task cannot be executed because there is nothing to migrate; no time was spent building a migration for a poller nobody ever wrote
